title: Load four Han-Modular modules into a HARTING hinged frame its spring holds open, then squeeze it shut until it clicks
instruction: Load the four modules into the hinged frame and close it until it clicks, then move both hands clear.
context: Electricians make up industrial connectors when wiring machines and control panels. O*NET 47-2111.00 Electricians, Core task: 'Assemble, install, test, or maintain electrical or electronic wiring, equipment, appliances, apparatus, or fixtures, using hand tools or power tools.' HARTING's Han-Modular instructions: 'install the completely assembled ... module in the Han-Modular hinged frame. Make sure that the module's notches fit into the recesses of the hinged frame' and 'close it by gently pressing on the outer sides of the frame'. The difficulty is physical: each 11 g wired module rests on the open frame's two support edges with about 1.5 mm of overlap, set at a 16 mm pitch beside the modules already standing, with finger pads wider than the pitch; then a squeeze must close the sprung frame round all four while every module stays seated. A module left high stops the click; one nudged off its edges drops through. A picture shows the positions, not how to set and keep them.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of the table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A HARTING Han hinged frame plus, size 16B (09 14 016 0361: 84.6 mm long over its end flanges, 34.4 mm across them, side walls 20 mm tall, 64 mm inside: four 16 mm positions A to D; zinc and stainless steel, 70 g), stands on a steel bench assembly stand (two 7 x 30 x 35 mm blocks under its end flanges, on a 110 x 50 x 2 mm plate), its foot 3.5 cm up, centred at (30, 0), long axis along x, positions A to D at x 27.6, 29.2, 30.8 and 32.4. Its two side walls are hinged at their feet and sprung 15 degrees open (0.3 N m/rad each); each has a 2.5 mm support edge along its inner foot and four windows with chamfered mouths. Four assembled Han E crimp modules (09 14 006 3001: 8 g, polycarbonate; 14.6 x 25 x 34 mm, a 5 x 2 x 6 mm lug on each face toward a wall), each with six crimp contacts fitted and their six 0.75 mm2 wires leaving its underside as a 30 mm tail (3 g with the contacts), stand on a plastic rack at x 20.5, 23, 25.5 and 28, y -16: two rails 11 cm long, 7 mm wide and 4.5 cm tall, 18 mm apart centre to centre, under the two ends of each module's foot, the tails hanging free between them, with 8 mm ribs on top between the modules.
scoring: By eye, caliper and video, read at the end of the run unless stated. Seated, frame open: a module let go (no fingertip within 5 mm of it) on both support edges at its position, within 1.5 mm along and across, its foot no more than 1.5 mm over the edges, and within 5 degrees of upright (engineer's square). Seated, frame shut: within 1 mm along, across and in height and 3 degrees, its lugs in their windows. Clicked: the latch heard, and the walls stay shut when let go. A position is empty when no module is within 8 mm along and 6 mm across of it, at any height (in, on or under the frame). 1.0: the frame closed and clicked with all four modules seated shut, every fingertip of both hands at least 3 cm from the frame and the modules, held 1 s. 0.6: closed and clicked with all four seated but a hand still within 3 cm, or with three seated, the fourth position empty and no module fallen through the frame, or all four seated with the hands clear for under 1 s. Closed and clicked otherwise: 0.075 for each module seated shut. Frame not closed: 0.075 for each module seated on the open frame (0.075 one, 0.15 two, 0.225 three, 0.3 all four). 0 if the frame was forced shut on a module more than 2 mm high (side-on video at the click), or a module fell off the table at any moment. Anything else scores 0.
reset_notes: The four modules back on the rack, their tails hanging between its rails, the frame open on its stand. No seed changes the scene.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz on GPU. Each wall is a hinge with a 0.3 N m/rad spring holding it 15 degrees open; the click is code: both walls within 0.5 degrees of shut lock. Each wire tail is one 30 mm, 3 g segment on a sprung joint bending across the frame (0.0005 N m/rad, 0.005 N m s/rad), cut short of a harness. Modules modelled 14.6 mm wide (a listing gives 15.5), 1.4 mm apart. The spring, support edges and tail stiffness are approximated, to be measured. The frame is fixed on its stand.
